asian_option_pricer.text: `bermudan_option_pricer` answers "what is an option worth if I can exercise early, but only on a few set dates?" `asian_option_pricer` answers "what is an option worth if its payoff depends on the average price over the life of the option?" The Bermudan prices an exercise right using the Longstaff-Schwartz regression method, with exercise allowed only on an evenly spaced subset of the time grid set by `exercise_dates`. Its price lies between the European and American values. The Asian pricer simulates paths and averages the observed prices (`n_steps` sets the number of observations), then pays off against `strike` at maturity. Averaging reduces volatility, so an Asian option is worth less than the matching vanilla European option. Both use Monte Carlo and take the same core inputs (`spot`, `strike`, `rate`, `sigma`, `tau`). The Bermudan defaults to a put and the Asian to a call.

explain.text: `bermudan_option_pricer` (the Bermudan Option Pricer) estimates the price of an option that can be exercised early, but only on a limited set of evenly spaced dates rather than at any time. It uses Longstaff-Schwartz Monte Carlo: simulated paths are stepped backward, and a regression decides at each allowed date whether exercising beats continuing. There is no closed form, so the result is a simulation estimate. The price sits between the European and American values. You supply `spot`, `strike`, `rate`, `sigma` and `tau`, and can set `exercise_dates`, `option_type` (call or put), `div_yield` and optionally `greeks`.

when.text:
The Bermudan Option Pricer (`bermudan_option_pricer`) fits when an option can be exercised early, but only on certain set dates.

- Use it for contracts with discrete exercise windows, where you set how many allowed dates there are with `exercise_dates`.
- It suits cases with no closed-form answer: it uses Longstaff-Schwartz Monte Carlo, so you control the accuracy trade-off through `n_simulations` and `n_steps`.
- It's useful as a sanity bracket, since the price lies between the European and American values.
- Calls or puts are supported via `option_type`, with `div_yield` for a dividend-paying underlying. Set `greeks` to true if you also want delta, gamma, vega, theta and rho.
- If the option can instead be exercised at any time, `american_option_lsm` is listed as the American option pricer using Longstaff-Schwartz Monte Carlo.
